note: Synthetic category pool and labelled ballot questions for the demo 5 router evaluation. Written by one author, not drawn from real ballots. 'acceptable' lists the pool categories a question is primarily about, generously where a reasonable voter would not object. 'squarely_inside' lists narrow categories the question sits squarely inside; their parent is always acceptable too.

categories.text: the well-being of tree frogs in the Amazon
street trees and the urban tree canopy
the fire department and ambulance service

questions.title: Senior property tax freeze
questions.summary: Freezes the assessed home value used for property tax for homeowners aged 65 and over with household income under $60,000.

questions.title: Property tax deferral for older homeowners
questions.summary: Lets homeowners aged 70 and over defer their property tax payments until the home is sold.

questions.title: Half-cent sales tax increase
questions.summary: Raises the city sales tax rate from 8.0 to 8.5 percent.

questions.title: Sales tax exemption for groceries
questions.summary: Removes the city sales tax on unprepared food.

questions.title: Hotel room tax
questions.summary: Adds a 3 percent tax on hotel and short-term rental stays.

questions.title: Business license tax restructuring
questions.summary: Replaces the flat business license fee with a tax based on gross receipts.

questions.title: Rainy day fund requirement
questions.summary: Requires the city to keep reserves equal to 10 percent of annual spending.

questions.title: Participatory budgeting pilot
questions.summary: Sets aside $2 million of the city budget each year for projects chosen directly by residents.

questions.title: Spending cap tied to tax revenue
questions.summary: Limits annual growth in city spending to the growth in tax revenue.

questions.title: Sister-city grant for Amazon amphibian habitat
questions.summary: Gives $150,000 to a partner city in Brazil to protect tree frog breeding habitat in the Amazon basin.

questions.title: Zoo conservation fund for Amazon tree frogs
questions.summary: Directs the city zoo to spend 1 percent of ticket revenue on tree frog conservation projects in the Amazon.

questions.title: Street tree planting bond
questions.summary: Borrows $12 million to plant and maintain 20,000 street trees.

questions.title: Protected tree ordinance
questions.summary: Requires a permit to remove any street tree or any large tree on private land.

questions.title: Single-use plastic bag ban
questions.summary: Bans single-use plastic bags at retail stores.

questions.title: City climate action plan
questions.summary: Commits the city to net-zero emissions from its own buildings and vehicles by 2040.

questions.title: Wetland restoration for stormwater
questions.summary: Restores 40 acres of wetland to absorb stormwater and reduce flooding.

questions.title: Lead water pipe replacement bond
questions.summary: Borrows $30 million to replace lead drinking water pipes.

questions.title: Sewer rate increase
questions.summary: Raises sewer rates by 6 percent a year for five years to rebuild the treatment plant.

questions.title: Free school breakfast and lunch
questions.summary: Provides free breakfast and lunch to every student in the public schools.

questions.title: Local produce in school cafeterias
questions.summary: Requires school cafeterias to buy 20 percent of the food for school lunches from local farms.

questions.title: School construction bond
questions.summary: Borrows $85 million to rebuild two elementary schools and repair school roofs across the district.

questions.title: Air conditioning for classrooms
questions.summary: Installs air conditioning in every public school building over four years.

questions.title: Later high school start times
questions.summary: Moves the high school start time from 7:30 to 8:45 a.m.

questions.title: Class size limit
questions.summary: Caps kindergarten through third grade classes at 20 students.

questions.title: School operating levy
questions.summary: Adds a property tax levy of $1.20 per $1,000 of assessed value to pay teacher salaries.

questions.title: Annual rent increase cap
questions.summary: Limits rent increases to 5 percent a year in buildings more than 15 years old.

questions.title: Just-cause eviction rule
questions.summary: Requires landlords to state one of nine approved reasons before ending a tenancy.

questions.title: Downtown height limit increase
questions.summary: Raises the maximum building height downtown from 6 to 12 stories.

questions.title: Height limit near the waterfront
questions.summary: Limits new buildings within 500 feet of the waterfront to 40 feet in height.

questions.title: Affordable housing bond
questions.summary: Borrows $50 million to build 600 income-restricted apartments.

questions.title: Legalizing backyard cottages
questions.summary: Allows one accessory dwelling unit on every residential lot.

questions.title: Transit-oriented development fund
questions.summary: Uses transit agency land next to stations for new housing and pays for better access to the stations.

questions.title: Protected bike lane network
questions.summary: Builds 25 miles of protected bike lanes on major streets.

questions.title: Bike lane on Main Street
questions.summary: Removes one car lane on Main Street to add a two-way protected bike lane.

questions.title: More frequent bus service
questions.summary: Funds buses every 10 minutes on the eight busiest routes.

questions.title: Free bus fares for youth
questions.summary: Makes city buses free for riders aged 18 and under.

questions.title: Street repaving bond
questions.summary: Borrows $40 million to repave 120 miles of streets and fill potholes.

questions.title: Lower residential speed limit
questions.summary: Lowers the speed limit on residential streets from 25 to 20 miles per hour.

questions.title: Civilian police review board
questions.summary: Creates an elected civilian board with the power to investigate complaints against police officers.

questions.title: Police inspector general
questions.summary: Creates an independent inspector general to audit police department policies and use of force.

questions.title: New fire station
questions.summary: Builds and staffs a new fire station in the north end.

questions.title: Ambulance response time standard
questions.summary: Requires the fire department to staff enough ambulances to reach 90 percent of calls within eight minutes.

questions.title: Hire more police officers
questions.summary: Funds 60 additional patrol officers.

questions.title: Gunshot detection system
questions.summary: Installs acoustic gunshot sensors in four neighborhoods.

questions.title: Paid sick leave
questions.summary: Requires employers to provide one hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked.

questions.title: Public health clinic funding
questions.summary: Funds two neighborhood clinics offering vaccinations and primary care.

questions.title: Flavored tobacco ban
questions.summary: Bans the sale of flavored tobacco and vaping products.

questions.title: Raise the minimum wage
questions.summary: Raises the city minimum wage to $19 an hour, then ties it to inflation.

questions.title: Minimum wage for tipped workers
questions.summary: Ends the lower minimum wage for tipped workers over three years.

questions.title: Predictable scheduling
questions.summary: Requires large retailers to post work schedules two weeks in advance.

questions.title: Heat protections for outdoor workers
questions.summary: Requires shade, water and rest breaks for outdoor workers when it is hotter than 90 degrees.

questions.title: Ranked choice voting for city offices
questions.summary: Uses ranked choice voting to elect the mayor and city council starting next year.

questions.title: Repeal ranked choice voting
questions.summary: Ends ranked choice voting and returns city elections to a primary and a top-two runoff.

questions.title: Move city elections to even years
questions.summary: Holds city elections in November of even-numbered years.

questions.title: Public campaign financing
questions.summary: Gives each voter four $25 vouchers to donate to candidates for city office.

questions.title: Parks levy renewal
questions.summary: Renews a property tax levy that funds park maintenance and community centers.

questions.title: New waterfront park
questions.summary: Converts a former shipping pier into a 9-acre public park.

questions.title: Woodland preserve and trails
questions.summary: Buys 200 acres of woodland for a nature preserve with public trails.

questions.title: Library hours expansion
questions.summary: Opens every branch library seven days a week.

questions.title: New central library bond
questions.summary: Borrows $60 million to replace the central library.

questions.title: No-kill animal shelter
questions.summary: Requires the city animal shelter to stop euthanizing adoptable animals.

questions.title: Pet license fee increase
questions.summary: Raises the annual dog license fee from $20 to $35 to fund the animal shelter.

questions.title: Municipal broadband utility
questions.summary: Creates a city-owned internet utility offering service to every household.

questions.title: Late-night noise limits
questions.summary: Lowers the allowed noise level for bars and music venues after 11 p.m.

questions.title: Extended bar hours
questions.summary: Lets bars in the entertainment district stay open until 4 a.m.

questions.title: New city flag
questions.summary: Adopts a new design for the official city flag.

questions.title: Official city song
questions.summary: Adopts 'Harbor Lights' as the official city song.

questions.title: Permanent standard time advisory vote
questions.summary: Advises the state legislature to adopt permanent standard time and end daylight saving time.
